title: Posy signaling messages (spec §2)
description: Every JSON control message defined in §2 of the Posy 1.0 spec, discriminated by the 't' field. They travel as UTF-8 JSON over the reliable, ordered signaling channel (WebSocket or a reliable data channel). Direction is noted in each definition. The 'examples' arrays are the examples from the spec text.

tier.description: Rate tier. Frequencies come from the 'tiers' map of the session message (spec example: FULL 30 Hz, NORMAL 15 Hz, MINIMAL 5 Hz). OFF stops forwarding.

transport.description: Pose-frame transport lane (spec §1.1, added in 1.0.5). 'sctp' is the primary WebRTC data channel; 'websocket' is the reliable-WebSocket fallback for server-relay deployments without native server-side WebRTC. Optional and backward-compatible: when absent on a message, that message's lane defaults to 'sctp' (the 1.0.0 default). The client states its lane in hello; the server confirms the authoritative accepted lane in session.

hello.description: Client → Server (§2.1). First message on the signaling channel. The uid is sent here and only here; it never appears inside a pose frame.

token.description: Authentication token. May be an empty string if the server does not require one.

protocol.description: Channel protocol string, "posy/1" for this version. A mismatching major version is answered with a BAD_VERSION error, so the schema only checks the shape.

session.description: Server → Client (§2.1). May be re-sent at any time to change authorization or playspace; clients apply it immediately.

epoch_unix_ms.description: Session epoch; timestamp_ms in pose frames counts from here.

allowed.description: Authoritative list of permitted data types. A client MUST NOT set a flag bit for a type not listed here.

ping.description: Client → Server (§2.2). t1 is the client's monotonic clock in milliseconds at send time.

pong.description: Server → Client (§2.2). Echoes t1 and adds ts, the server's session-clock time in milliseconds.

peers.description: Server → Client (§2.3). Maps data consumers to uids; identity is carried by the channel, not the packet. At least one of 'add' / 'remove' must be present (the spec example has both) — enforced with minProperties: 't' plus at least one more.

subscribe.description: Client → Server (§2.4). Chooses the rate tier for one peer; also the congestion fallback.

rate.description: Server → Client (§2.4). The highest tier currently demanded by any of the sender's subscribers, in Hz. Senders MUST NOT exceed it (+10% tolerance).

error.description: Server → Client (§2.5). Error handling is server-enforced. 'action' is free-form text in 1.0-draft (the only value that appears in the spec is the example "POSE_MUTED").
